relevanceRationale.presentDay: Number arithmetic and reduction remain supported.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Means are a concrete aggregation operation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Empty identities, precision and preserving observations transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded finite inputs make the foundation exercise explicit.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Type and rounding checks prevent modest aggregation mistakes.

defects: The original brief did not define the numeric domain, rounding or input preservation.
Cent-rounded results passed the original finite fixtures.
An intermediate new tolerance fixture coerced decimal string results; an executable counterexample prompted an explicit numeric guard.

Fractional fixtures check a numeric result within a small tolerance, accepting the independently written online-mean alternative while rejecting rounding and string-valued decimal results. The explanation names 0/0 specifically instead of claiming every division by zero is NaN. Frozen/mutable input and the 10,000-item bound are exercised.

objective: Filter primitive strings by stored UTF-16 length while preserving order and occurrences.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Length-based selection is a practical collection operation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Code-unit versus visual-character reasoning transfers to text handling.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The supplied UTF-16 rule fits a JavaScript length exercise.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Explicit units and multiplicity prevent modest text-selection mistakes.

defects: The word characters did not say whether it meant UTF-16 units, code points or visible graphemes.
Code-point filtering and deduplication passed all ASCII-only fixtures.
Fresh-result and read-only input policies were previously implicit rather than clearly stated.
rationale: The new contract deliberately uses String.length units, including an explicit two-unit emoji example. Unicode pairs, combining sequences, empty strings and duplicates distinguish the stated rule from code-point counting. Reference/filter, push loop, named-boundary helper and independent reduce pass. Fresh empty/all-matching arrays and unchanged frozen/mutable inputs are required explicitly; this is a clarified policy, not a claim that Unicode code-point filtering was unambiguously forbidden before.

objective: Enumerate own enumerable string keys in JavaScript order without depending on the object's prototype.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Object.keys and reflection are supported primitives.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Object metadata enumeration is a direct engineering task.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Ownership, enumerability and key kinds transfer to object APIs.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Explicit ordinary data objects keep the reflection lesson bounded.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Safe enumeration prevents real crashes on null/shadowed prototypes.

defects: Insertion-order wording was false for array-index keys.
The junior solution called object.hasOwnProperty directly and failed null-prototype or shadowed-method records.
Non-enumerable/symbol exclusions and mutable input preservation lacked meaningful fixtures.
rationale: The brief now states array-index ordering followed by other strings in creation order, filters own/enumerable/string traits and admits null prototypes. The junior enumerates Reflect.ownKeys with a borrowed propertyIsEnumerable check. Reference and entries-based senior stay valid. Numeric index boundaries, hidden/symbol keys, own __proto__/constructor fields, null prototypes and mutable/frozen inputs are checked.

objective: Shallow-copy own enumerable data safely, preserving references and overriding the active flag without mutating input.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Shallow object copying is supported modern JavaScript.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Immutable record updates are a concrete application operation.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Ownership, overwrite order and shallow identity transfer.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The own-enumerable data contract makes all variants teach one operation.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Avoiding proto setters and nested mutation prevents substantive correctness hazards.

defects: The junior for-in copy included inherited fields, omitted symbols and mishandled own __proto__ data.
The Object.assign-to-plain-target senior invoked the inherited proto setter rather than preserving a data key.
Nested reference/mutation and fresh already-active results were insufficiently checked.
rationale: The reference spread remains correct. Junior explicitly defines own enumerable string/symbol data properties; senior assigns into a null-prototype target with no inherited __proto__ setter. Tests preserve nested identity and state, exclude inherited/non-enumerable fields, keep symbol keys and own __proto__ data, and require a fresh already-active result. The independent fromEntries alternative passes; JSON cloning, mutation and plain-target assignment fail.
